canonical.name: The vanishing sets define the Zariski topology on the prime spectrum, and every Zariski-open set is covered by distinguished opens that refine at points.
The prime-spectrum construction is contravariantly functorial on topological spaces, and quotient and localisation spectra are realised as the expected closed and open subspaces.
The prime spectrum is compact, and every distinguished open subset is compact in the same non-Hausdorff sense.
The closure of a prime is its vanishing set, specialisation is reverse inclusion, prime spectra are T0, and the closed points are exactly the maximal ideals.
A Zariski-closed subset is irreducible exactly when its radical defining ideal is prime, with irreducible components corresponding to minimal primes.
A Noetherian ring has Noetherian spectrum, and therefore only finitely many irreducible components.
Clopen decompositions of the spectrum correspond to nontrivial idempotents, so the spectrum is connected exactly when the ring has no idempotents other than zero and one.
The support of any module is stable under specialisation, and in affine finite-type spectra the closed points are dense in every closed subset.
